directive:
Revise only the framing and certificates; preserve the fixed-0<e<1 all-generator iff theorem and its quantified scope.

1. Correct every Jung–Kang source reference in the bibliography, comparator claim, related_work, literature checklist, and seed/opened-evidence fields from “Theorem 1 / Appendix B” to “Assumption 4; Theorem 5, equations (3)–(4); proof in Appendix E.” Do not alter references to this proposal’s own Theorem 1. Describe Jung–Kang’s contribution precisely: Theorem 5 proves that every compatible interventional law lies in the propensity-calibrated f-divergence ambiguity class, and their later optimization is exact relative to that ambiguity class. It does not establish that every member of the class is realizable by a bow SCM. Replace the claim that they “treat the radius as a sharp causal feasible set” with neutral language distinguishing ambiguity-class extrema (valid outer causal bounds) from sharp extrema over the compatible bow-SCM fiber. If the class is called the “Jung–Kang ball,” note that the proposal uses its mutual-absolute-continuity version under Assumption 4; equation (10) itself visibly states only P<<Q, while the maintained model and density parametrization supply the reverse domination.

2. Repair honest_scope without changing thm:generator-iff-frontier: extend only the mixture/SCM class and endpoint maps to e=1, where M_1(P)=L_1(P)={P} and L_1(p)=U_1(p)=p. Delete the assertion that every calibrated divergence ball is {P}. A zero-radius f-ball is a singleton only under an additional strict Jensen-equality/cap-detecting condition; affine and identically-zero generators are counterexamples. Keep the iff theorem explicitly at fixed 0<e<1.

3. Make thm:generator-iff-frontier the sole flagship headline. Present bow-mixture completeness as its structural input, the open-illegal theorem as its stable converse, and the CDF/query/inference results as consequences or implementation layers rather than co-equal novelty claims.

4. Add two explicit binary certificates. For KL, fix any p in (0,1), let P=Bern(p), q_0=ep, and Q_epsilon=Bern(ep-epsilon). Show D_KL(P||Bern(q_0)) = p log(1/e)+(1-p)log((1-p)/(1-ep)) < -log e=B_KL(e). Hence, by continuity, every sufficiently small epsilon>0 keeps D_KL(P||Q_epsilon)<B_KL(e), while p/(ep-epsilon)>1/e, so Q_epsilon is ball-feasible but SCM-illegal. For the propensity hinge f_c(t)=(t-c)_+, c=1/e, show B_f(e)=0 and, for P=Bern(p), Q=Bern(q), D_f(P||Q)=(p-cq)_+ + ((1-p)-c(1-q))_+. Thus D_f(P||Q)=0 iff ep<=q<=1-e+ep, exactly the binary mixture fiber. State that positive scaling and addition of b(t-1) leave this certificate unchanged.

Retain the remaining theorem statements unless a later proof audit finds a genuine failure; do not broaden the SCM or generator assumptions in this revision.
